column7: We traveled about 4 hours Friday to my father in laws this weekend and she literally did not use the potty at all since we left.
Since we have been home though she is refusing to even sit on the potty and try to pee.
My three year old ONLY wants me for literally anything. Potty. Meals. Snacks. Comfort. Entertainment. Bath time. Bedtime.
Tonight my husband tried to take him upstairs for a bath so I could get ready for the week, and now I’m sitting by the bathtub because neither of them could handle it.
my dear husband is trying his best but I feel like his confidence is shot at this point. Any time he tries to help or take the lead, my son has a total breakdown and I have to step in.
you’re right by saying that me stepping in is reinforcing the behavior, and my son is worse when I’m home and my husband is taking the lead.
my son has to learn that we’re BOTH his parents. Not just mom and her assistant.
A lot of it seems like boundary pushing but no matter how hard we hold the boundary he just is not breaking through.
column8: Father of a 4-year-old with months of bedtime fights.

column7: We have tried negative reinforcement (taking things away each time he gets out of bed), positive reinforcement (sticker chart with substantial rewards at even small milestones like two good nights), check in system, cry it out
It’s like some switch flipped soon after turning 4 and we cannot unflip it or get back to a baseline. What am I missing?
We have done all of this. It has not resolved.
column8: Reply to a list of standard advice.

column7: daycare makes all the kids lay down on cots
column8: Daycare nap affects bedtime; work sets dinner time.

column7: Dinner is at 5:30-6 and lights out is 7:30. We can’t do dinner any earlier because of work.
We've tried rewards, taking things away, being nice, I've gotten angry (I told him sorry, please don't judge me)
column8: 2y9m boy, five months of pee accidents.

column7: I truly am at my wits end, I can't do his laundry daily and dealing with constant accidents. Is he just not ready? Do I put him back in diapers for a while?
He also has massive fomo and constantly says "I'm going to miss" about whatever he's doing, we've told him everything is paused so he can go pee
He even went and licked an apple.  So I had to buy a single apple no one in our house likes and is slightly soft cause my son licked it.   I am burnt out and just done.
column8: Grocery trip after days at a sick relative's bedside.

column7: He hasn't been listening to me all day.  But when it counted he listen.
We are 7 weeks into potty training my 2yo (26mos) and followed the Oh Crap method. I followed to a T, he did amazing, I was so proud, and then it all changed.
column8: Constant pee accidents seven weeks in.

column7: Sometimes underwear helps, which is against the oh crap method, but he likes wearing them and I only give him one chance
He’s excited about it too, “mommy, pee in shorts” “mommy, pee on floor” “mommy, pee in car seat” like ugh what do I do?
I’ve started setting timers and making him go, and then somehow he pees his pants 5min later.
It's also always me, if me and his dad are in the same room it's only ever me that he will climb all over and shove a toy truck into my face.
I just want 2 minutes a day where I dont have to pretend I'm absolutely loving being handed random objects.
I can already hear the suggestions - its separation anxiety! He just wants to be around you all the time! I am very confident that is not the case.
We just got him a water table with all these different pipes and valves, he just throws rocks in it lmao.
column8: Toys bought to encourage independent play.

column7: I'll keep looking for more stuff he can get stuck into, throwing toys at the problem clearly isnt helping.
My 2 y/o is impulsive and is so difficult to redirect. I get it - typical toddler behavior. But with a crying newborn on top of getting kicked and constantly touched, I am so over it.
column8: Mother four weeks after a second birth.

column7: I know many parents will say, "Just stop giving it to her," but when I try, she will cry endlessly.
column8: Weaning a 15-month-old off the bedtime bottle.

column7: I'm looking for advice on how to slowly wean her off the bottle without making bedtime a complete disaster. Has anyone successfully done this with a very strong-willed toddler?
Between him, our almost 2-year-old, and our 4-month-old, I felt completely overwhelmed and honestly wanted to cry.
column8: Grocery trip with three boys; the 4-year-old ran around.

column7: He recently said the F-word at daycare, and his teacher had to let us know.
At this point I am clueless on discipline you try to talk to him , give him time out , take somthing away that  he loves. He still will get upset.
I never noticed this kind of behavior when we had our second child, but with our third I've seen a big difference in just a few short months.
column8: The third baby as the trigger.

column7: He says I'm too soft when it comes to discipline, but I just don't want to hurt my child.
column8: Her husband's view of her discipline.

column7: They require pull ups until fully accident free for two weeks
column8: Daycare rules for a 22-month-old doing Oh Crap.

column7: They don’t allow squaty potties (what we have been using) only toilet with insert
I’m feeling torn about how to attempt this situation to minimize regression. Has anyone sent their kid back to daycare with it being two days a week only?

I find it really unlikely my daughter will be able to communicate to a teacher she has to pee anytime soon as she can’t even do that with us. And how can she self initiate if the toilet in a different room is another option. It feels destined to screw her up.
My strategy as of now is basically handing them the keys. But keeping what we do at home the same with no pull ups only commando for awhile
We redirect her when she runs away by holding her hand which causes her to have a meltdown, screaming and crying and biting our hands.
column8: First-time mother of a 14-month-old who runs off.

column7: We firmly say "No" and "No biting" but it seems futile.
I think I may need to invest in a good toddler harness for her. We have a little backpack harness for her and she will do the dead weight thing
Daycare was supportive and said they were happy to follow whatever we did at home
The problem started about two weeks ago when he moved daycare classrooms to the next class up.
The ratio of students to toddlers increased. His old classroom has two teachers in the room, and the new one only has one.
The teacher that's in his classroom in the morning is very understanding and patient, but the teacher that's there in the afternoon seems overwhelmed and often sends him home in a diaper.
column8: It depends on which teacher is on.

column7: I've tried several different potty seats, and they're all too big to fit on the classroom's toilet seat.
column8: Seats bought for the new classroom toilet.

column7: When I'm finally done doing it I'll shake my head and tell her "no, Mommy's all done playing that game, I'm gonna \[insert activity here\] now." This is unacceptable.
column8: Stay-at-home mother of a 2-year-old and a 1-year-old.

column7: You can say "hide the toy", whatever toy she's wanting me to play with, but then when she can't find it she just throws a tantrum over that.
Changing the game is not an option for her, she does not want anything else, she wants one specific thing and if it's not done, then it's a tantrum.
Daycare has shared with us that it originated from one child and spread throughout the room, so it’s an ongoing problem with almost every toddler in the room.
column8: Almost-2-year-old hitting since the toddler-room move.

column7: She doesn’t do it when she is angry or upset, she does it and then laughs about it.
We both just read the book how to talk so little kids will listen and we are trying to implement the verbiage.

Reading books, positive narration when she’s being gentle, saying that hands are not for hitting and giving ideas of what we can do with our hands instead, leaving the room, removing her from the situation, taking breaks
And I think the failure is really on my part and not on hers.
column8: Daughter nearly 3 still in pull-ups; older brother trained by 2.5.

column7: I remember all the cleaning up and the work that went into potty training her brother, and so I’ve just been procrastinating with her.
I’ve been so busy with work and momming that it’s also just hard to find the time to really dedicate to this. But that’s not an excuse.
She will go pee on the potty at preschool too, according to her teachers.
more so just venting my mom failure guilt. Her brother was basically daytime potty trained by 2.5 and she is now past that point.
We used the Oh Crap method with my first in the beginning, but honestly we didn't love everything about that book.
We were too high strung about it with my oldest. We got there in the end, but only after we relaxed and stopped putting so much pressure on all of us to get it right.
column8: Looking back at the first child's training.

column7: How do we potty train a nonverbal child? We can't have a back-and-forth discussion about the situation, and that's what's throwing me off here.
I think maybe it's because it's sort of the last line between babyhood and childhood for many kids, I guess. But also, totally, no one wants to clean up accidents!
